title: Three Seasons and One Short Brush
subtitle: 艺术殿堂 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 艺术殿堂（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）
meta: 主题语境：艺术殿堂（文学艺术与体育·绘画、建筑等领域的代表作品和人物）　|　核心词汇：portrait　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 portrait 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1963 the painter ① painted the portrait that no visitor in the studio would have noted, and he said the painting was the whole of the season. The ② portrait, meaning the picture itself and not the brush, ran three seasons and stayed unnoted in the book; a portrait, he said, is the only thing in a studio that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ portrait in that studio had the same short brush beside it, and the ④ portrait at the far easel, meaning the sketch they kept for the children to keep and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A portrait, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the painter said the noting is the part that fills three seasons.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the portrait was the whole of the matter, meaning the likeness and not the picture. The ⑥ portrait, meaning the likeness and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; portrait, he said, is either something you paint or the only word that means both a picture and a likeness. He said the likeness is the part they remember.

By 1968 the ⑦ portrait had become a line in a catalogue, and the catalogue had become an argument about the short brush. The ⑧ portrait of the whole thing, the painter wrote in May, was one studio and three seasons of noting; portrait, he said, is either the sketch at the far easel or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ portrait I remember is the picture noted in the catalogue, which closed in 1970 and is still noted as the quietest in the studio. A ⑩ portrait, my mother said in 1972, is the only picture that improves by being noted; every portrait, she said, is a likeness that has agreed to look like a picture. She said the likeness was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 肖像；画像（指画室里每一幅旁边的那一幅）
B. n. 肖像；画像（指那幅肖像本身，与小小的画笔相对）
C. 固定搭配：paint the portrait 画这一幅肖像
D. n. 肖像；画像（指留给孩子们留着的那一幅）
E. n. 肖像之事（抽象总称，指一处画室的肖像之事）
F. n. 肖像；画像（指展品目录里写到、被记下的那一幅）
G. n. 肖像、神似（指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 神似（抽象总称，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: painted the portrait that no visitor in the studio would have noted
The portrait, meaning the picture itself and not the brush
the portrait at the far easel

answers.why: paint the portrait 意为“画这一幅肖像”，1963 年那位画师把画室里没有一位观者肯记下的一幅肖像做了一遍。
portrait 意为“肖像；画像”，指那幅肖像本身而不是小小的画笔，它经过了三个季度而在簿子上没有被记下。
portrait 意为“肖像；画像”，指画室里每一幅旁边的那一幅，每一幅旁边都有同一支小小的画笔。
portrait 意为“肖像；画像”，指最远那副画架的留给孩子们留着的那一幅，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
portrait 意为“肖像、神似”，指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这幅神似就是那件事的全部。
portrait 意为“神似”，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西而不是那幅肖像，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
portrait 意为“肖像；画像”，指展品目录里写到、被记下的那一幅，到 1968 年这一幅成了展品目录里的一行。
portrait 意为“肖像之事”，画师五月写道，整件事的肖像之事是一处画室和三个季度的记下。
portrait 意为“肖像；画像”，我记得的是展品目录里记下过的那一幅，1970 年画成了，至今仍被说成画室里最安静的一幅。
portrait 为抽象总称，母亲 1972 年说，肖像是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的肖像。
